Femjun is a very direct reference to Femshep, the female version of Commander Shepard in BioWare's Mass Effect trilogy. While the male version was effectively the default playable character through the first two games, BioWare took steps to put them on equal footing for Mass Effect 3. That effort included a vote to let fans decide the character's official face , which was subsequently used on alternate or inside covers of Mass Effect 3 packaging. 

Voiced by Jennifer Hale, Femshep became so popular that when BioWare dropped the Mass Effect Legendary Edition trailer, it was she who appeared most prominently .

So, back to Exodus: Fenjum will be portrayed by Carina Conti, who's appeared in television shows including Tracker, Good Trouble, All Rise, and Winning Time: The Rise of the Lakers Dynasty. items.title: The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping Review
items.summary:
The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping is in theaters on November 20. 

The last 14 years have featured a lot of big screen Reapings as YA novelist Suzanne Collins’ dystopian The Hunger Games books have been adapted into six individual films. A franchise based on children murdering one another doesn’t exactly scream “blockbuster hit,” but Collins’ reluctant heroine Katniss Everdeen (as embodied by Jennifer Lawrence) captured the hearts and minds of Millennial readers and moviegoers, and so the franchise goes on. 

Under the uninterrupted guidance of producer Nina Jacobson and executive producer/director Francis Lawrence, Collins’ surprise standalone prequel books, The Ballad of Songbirds & Snakes and Sunrise on the Reaping, have also been adapted into big budget movies. The former revealed Coriolanus Snow’s (Tom Blyth) origin story before he turned into a white-haired, totalitarian child killer (Donald Sutherland), while the latter and latest explains the cascading tragedies that created Panem’s lore around Second Quarter Quell victor Haymitch Abernathy, and ultimately why he mentored Katniss and Peeta (Josh Hutcherson) the way he did after their Reaping 24 years later. 

While Woody Harrelson brought the perennially sauced Haymitch to vivid life in the first four Hunger Games films, the details about what prompted the character to retreat into booze and solitude primarily remained a mystery. That alone is a decent reason to add another chapter to the franchise — fleshing out the beloved character and giving him his due — but there’s also an equally strong case against…

items.title: Valve-sanctioned Half-Life remake Black Mesa gets a mondo update and a Steam Deck verified badge
items.summary:
Here's a terrifying reminder that the cold hand of Death is on my shoulder: I'm pretty sure I first played Black Mesa back in 2012, at the tender age of 19. In the intervening 14 years, the fan-made Half-Life 1 remake has walked quite the road, including getting Valve's official blessing to sell itself—for money!—on Steam in 2015.

And they're still going, the mad lads. Just yesterday, Black Mesa got a hefty major update "featuring visual upgrades, engine optimizations, and a complete interface overhaul". It's called the Anomalous Improvements Update and it's a real humdinger.

The biggest improvement—if you are me, a man who tries to play basically everything on his Steam Deck these days—is the Steam Deck verification and much-improved controller support. The game will now recognise and let you use a gamepad right from the jump, rather than forcing you to faff around in settings, and generally seems like a rather seamless delight on Deck in the little bit of time I've mucked about with it.

Black Mesa's also been optimised "to deliver significantly better performance across the entire game". By way of evidence, the devs show a side-by-side of Gordon Freeman hanging out in Xen. Pre-update, he gets ~130 fps. Post-update, he gets ~170. Now, admittedly, both of these framerates fall into a category I like to call "absolutely fine", but it's always nice to squeeze a little more juice out of a game.

items.title: What would Rockstar have done if GTA hadn't taken off? Former tech director Obbe Vermeij on Scottish zombies, James Bond and the "curse" of success
items.summary:
It's bizarre today to think of Rockstar working on games that aren't Grand Theft Auto . Frankly, it's bizarre to think of Rockstar working on games that aren't GTA 6 , which rolls onto console hard drives this week. A decade in the making, with a development team of thousands scattered across an international network of studios, GTA 6 aims to be the Maximum Game. It's both a dense, lively open world and a monument to the exhausting impersonality of "triple-A" game productions. It contains multitudes: birdlife! Realistic cloud formation! Fuel mechanics! Romance! Soda visibly sloshing around in bottles! It's an imperial production shadowed by labour disputes , that appears to have given Rockstar's various teams little time or space to think about anything else.

It wasn't ever thus. Once upon a time, Rockstar weren't just known for GTA and to a considerably lesser extent, Red Dead Redemption . Once upon a time, they had a reputation for slightly dodgy experiments. I recently interviewed former Rockstar North tech director Obbe Vermeij about a few of them, including Agent, the unofficial James Bond game Rockstar toyed with before putting all chips on Grand Theft Auto 5 .
items.t: What would Rockstar have done if GTA hadn't taken off? Former tech director Obbe Vermeij on Scottish zombies, James Bond and the "curse" of success

items.title: Civilization dev Firaxis reportedly lays off a third of its staff, studio head departs
items.summary:
A Bloomberg report says Civilization studio Firaxis has laid off roughly 60 people, representing about one-third of its total headcount. Heather Hazen, who took over as studio head in 2023 after more than 25 years with Firaxis, is also leaving.

A 2K Games spokesperson didn't comment on the reported number of employees let go, but confirmed that layoffs had occurred in a statement provided to PC Gamer. "Firaxis is restructuring and recentering around the studio’s core strength — designing world class strategy games that have set the industry standard for the genre for the last 30 years," the rep said.

"As part of these changes, the size of the studio is being reduced to focus on design, technology and the player experience, which means saying goodbye to talented colleagues who helped build Firaxis. These decisions are never easy, but they’re essential to build the next chapter of Firaxis."

The rep also confirmed that Hazen has stepped down as Firaxis studio head: "With the studio entering this reset, she feels this is the right, deliberate moment to hand over the reins to ensure the next studio leader has full ownership of this new era from the start."

Firaxis has enjoyed great success as the developer of the Civilization and XCOM games, but it's struggled in recent years. Marvel's Midnight Suns was critically acclaimed but sales were middling, while Civilization 7 was just middling overall: Despite a raft of updates and changes since its 2025 release, its user rating on Steam remains stubbornly "mixed" while player numbers are still well behind that of Civilization 6.…

"I did not live up to the standards expected of everyone at Nvidia, and I have made serious mistakes in my personal life. I created problems for the Board that I deeply regret," Huang says.

"If the Board of Directors decides that my return is in the best interest of our shareholders, our employees, the company, and America, I would be honored to answer these calls and return as CEO."

President Donald Trump and a cohort of silicon valley execs have previously backed the Nvidia co-founder, even if Trump did wobble his way over to backing ex-Apple CEO Tim Cook for a day. A heap of signatures were also added to a #bringjensenback petition , supposedly including Elon Musk and Tim Sweeney. Sweeney has barely come up for air he's so wound up about Huang's resignation. 

Yet all these big names won't mean much if Huang can't convince the company's board of directors.

Last we heard, Nvidia's board was intent on moving past Huang . That's according to someone close to the matter speaking to CNBC . There are also a lot of things hanging over Huang at the moment, including an internal investigation at Nvidia, a couple of chats with Congress , an ongoing investigation into Nvidia's customer, Megaspeed , and any potential share price shock as markets would react to the news.

items.title: Kevin Smith Explains How Marvel and Star Wars Collide in Hope Assembles Crossover

Marvel Comics is kicking off 2027 with one of the most unexpected projects we've ever seen from the publisher. Star Wars/Marvel: Hope Assembles brings these two iconic universes together at long last, as the classic cast of Star Wars: A New Hope suddenly appears in the present-day Marvel Universe. The whole thing is overseen by two creators with plenty of nerdy bona fides: writer Kevin Smith (Clerks) and artist David Marquez (Miles Morales: Ultimate Spider-Man). 

IGN recently had a chance to chat briefly with Smith to find out more about how this massive crossover came to be and which team-ups he's most enjoying. Read on to learn more.

As you might expect, Smith was as taken aback as anyone when he was first approached by Marvel to pitch for the series. It took a bit of thinking and soul-searching before he arrived at what he felt was the right approach for this story.

"I was honored but hesitant," Smith tells IGN. "Playing with someone else’s toys, you run the risk of upsetting folks who hold these characters near and dear — so I gave it a second before I said yes, weighing the possible pros and cons. items.title: 'I want to be clear, I want people to have a lot of RAM' says Sam Altman, weeks after seeming to say the opposite
items.summary:
Sam Altman, the CEO of OpenAI, got in hot water late last month when he said, "From a global allocation perspective, actually it’s quite terrible to have everyone have a bunch of the world’s limited supply of DRAM sitting in their own computer, and be used 5% of the time". He has since gone on to say he wants everyone to have RAM, actually, and in a conversation with Semafor , he has elaborated on what he claims he actually means (via The Verge ).

Altman says, "I want to be clear, I want people to have a lot of RAM. I think everybody should buy a lot of RAM, be able to buy a lot of RAM for their own computer. I think this is good. I think the home tinkering is great."

So why the discrepancy? Altman says his comment was "misinterpreted, but there is a true part of it". He argues that the optimal way to use memory is to share it (in this case, he seems to be referring to the use of AI in home rigs), and "have it working 100% of the time. Rather than, like, sometimes off in someone's Edge device."

So I guess if we all share RAM, we get more at the end of the day. I'll wait for OpenAI to share its memory with me, and then I might do the same. 

Altman points out that he got in more trouble a few years ago for saying there would be "a huge squeeze on memory". He then notes that many didn't believe it would be such a worry, and "we have seen DRAM prices, I don't know exactly, but maybe they went up like 5x, 7x or something like that. items.title: TCL CSOT's new OLED panels might not only be cheaper, but also have high refresh rates and hassle-free pixel burn-in compensation
items.summary:
I've had my eye on TCL CSOT—CSOT being a TCL subsidiary responsible for OLED production—for a while now. It might just be the company that brings OLED monitor prices down thanks to its use of the inkjet-printing (IJP) process in manufacturing. TCL CSOT had already said it was moving in equipment for IJP manufacturing and expected production in the fourth quarter of 2027, but the company is now showing off some pretty impressive panels made using the process.

According to Display Specifications (via TechPowerUp ), at the Display Tech-Ecosystem Conference 2026 (DTC2026), TCL CSOT showed off a 27-inch, 1440p, 500 Hz gaming monitor made using IJP tech. Apparently, the company describes this monitor as having the "world's first high-refresh-rate in-panel compensation system."

You already knew what that was, right? No, me either. According to Display Specification's understanding of the announcement, it's tech that "continuously adjusts image performance in the background without requiring periodic compensation cycles while the display is powered off."

OLED pixels can degrade at different rates, which is what causes pixel burn-in. The usual method for solving this is to run compensation cycles while the display is off, which takes a few minutes and boosts underperforming pixels up a bit back to where they should be. 

It sounds like TCL's new tech will somehow allow this to happen without turning the monitor off, and will just happen as it's being used. Which might compensate for pixel burn-in without as much hassle. Just bear in mind that the word here is "compensation", not…

items.title: AMD introduces Capacity Aware Scheduling to the Linux kernel, which sure is the thing I'd do if I were introducing Zen 6 LP cores next year
items.summary:
AMD's Vishal Badole recently posted two Linux kernel patches (via TechPowerUp ), and these both pair up to introduce Capacity Aware Scheduling (CAS) for AMD heterogeneous processors. If that sounds like gibberish to you, effectively, this lays the groundwork to more efficiently handle AMD chips that have different core types. 

Up until now, AMD's performance scaling driver for Linux (amd-pstate) treated all cores as equal, assigning tasks regardless of core strength. AMD's current heterogeneous design pairs full-fat Zen 5 and lower-caste Zen 5C cores together in Zen 5 chips nowadays, but there is far less actual difference between these two core types than in the P-cores and E-cores of modern Intel architectures. 

But Zen 6's full lineup is currently suggested to be quite different. Also shared in a Linux patch earlier this year , Zen 6 is set to introduce a new Low Power core type (which is set to run at a very low power, as you might guess from the name), and that is a core type that would really benefit from Capacity Aware Scheduling. 

What AMD has called Performance and Efficiency cores up until now is not the same as what Intel has called Performance and Efficiency cores. AMD's Efficiency cores are effectively just compact versions of the Performance cores, whereas Intel's E and P cores have different microarchitectures and are specifically tailored for different use cases. 

The new Zen 6 LP cores appear to be similar to Intel's LPE (Low Power Efficiency) cores you will find in its Panther Lake chips . And as such, the need for CAS makes more sense. If AMD LP…

items.title: Ex-Call of Duty live service manager joins EA as the new GM of Battlefield

It could be a glint atop the mountains on Liberation Peak, reliving the launch of Battlefield 2042 , or maybe it's the randomised recoil from the first Battlefield. All of these are good bets, but I think the real shared nightmare of most Battlefield players is that someday it'll morph into Call of Duty . 

To be fair, this fear isn't entirely unfounded. Bryan Beede was previously appointed as Battlefield's general manager after spending 19 years working on Call of Duty and has now been promoted to group general manager at EA. Kurtaj's hack of Rockstar was notable not for the GTA 6 infodump that followed, but because of how it was carried out: With an Amazon Fire Stick , a mobile phone, and a Bluetooth keyboard and mouse, connected to a TV in a Travelodge hotel room where he was being held under police protection because of threats against him made by rival hackers over stolen bitcoin.

A 2023 assessment found Kurtaj had "acute autism" and was determined to return to "cybercrime" as soon as possible, despite the fact that he was literally standing trial for doing cybercrimes. Because of that, the jury was asked to determine if he had committed the hacks (it found he had) but not whether he had done so with criminal intent; he was subsequently sentenced to an indefinite stay at a secure hospital , where he would remain unless and until doctors determined that he was no longer a danger.

As we noted at the time, "danger" might seem a bit of a strong word for someone who leaked videogame footage, but the Lapsus$ group had also hacked Microsoft , Samsung , Nvidia and UK telecom company BT&EE, and stole millions in cryptocurrency from individuals. items.title: Spirit Crossing, the new Zelda-ish hangout MMO from the creators of Cozy Grove, understands that sometimes you just want to be alone
items.summary:
New multiplayer game Spirit Crossing offers up a visually blissful, but inwardly draconian world in which other people are not allowed to talk to you – indeed, not permitted access to the visible electromagnetic spectrum – unless you have given them a high five. By default, players appear to each other as shadows, all exploring a skybound landscape of magic animals and layer-cake mountains that reminds me of both Sable and The Legend of Zelda: Tears of the Kingdom.

Deign to slap somebody's hand, and they'll pop into colour and be able to join you for various activities. For example, going fishing, playing instruments round the campfire, playing dress-up and pulling emotes in group photos, bouncing around on strangely inflated yaks, or questing forth to heal troubled spirits. There's some material gathering and crafting, and there are recurring storms that make the ambience more threatening, but overcoming a challenge doesn't feel like the point of Spirit Crossing. The "missions" are just an excuse to hang out together.

We know, at the very least, that director and producer Naoki Yoshida has been thinking about ways to make that barrier to entry a little less frightening— he said as much during Final Fantasy 14's Berlin Fan Festival —but according to a recent Letter from the Producer , it turns out we could've actually had something as recently as August.

"The idea of letting players freely choose a starting point for their adventure has been discussed, with the goal being to offer players a range of choices, rather than prescribe their experience according to my philosophy," Yoshida wrote.

Story skips are locked to the cash shop and, up until now, never included the current expansion. He's repeatedly expressed the fact that he's not too keen on letting people jump in wherever they feel, since it kinda mucks up the decade-plus worldbuilding and character relationships the game has built.

When you pick yourself up, you are inside a vast attic full of books and bricabrac, lit from one side by windows that offer no view of the outside world – just light and mist.

Tarnation! You have been lured into the eternal prison of Sunday Afternoon. Fortunately, there are several ways to escape.
